title: CrossWave kernel mismatch — remediation plan and regression guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a capacity surge on 2026-03-04 we observed sustained p95/p99 latency regressions on mixed-length traffic. Investigation showed the scheduler began selecting a crosswave kernel variant optimized for short sequences for a non-trivial fraction of long-sequence requests (>= 2k tokens), causing attention autotiling to fall back to a slow path and triggering KV cache churn. This ticket captures the remediation steps, short-term mitigations, telemetry additions, and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
root_cause_summary: An interaction between a recent heuristic change in the scheduler's path scorer and a fallback weight update in the kernel catalog caused misclassification of sequence-length buckets under bursty traffic. The scheduler favored a low-latency short-seq kernel when its internal moving-average latency metric was skewed by a transient spike of short requests; when long requests hit those worker assignments the kernel's slow attention fallback increased tail latency significantly.
impact: Customer-facing latency regressions across hosted API and several dedicated pools during peak windows; several customer threads reported timeouts and increased token charges due to retries. Estimated 12% p99 increase on affected pools during the incident window.

2026-03-04 09:26: on-call paged; traffic routing confirmed healthy; initial mitigation: increased worker pool margin

actions: A1: Pin scheduler path-scorer weights to v2026-02-25 baseline in prod configs (owner: Miguel Torres, due: 2026-03-13) - short-term rollback to stop regressions
A2: Add per-kernel per-sequence-length histograms and 1/5/15min moving averages to tracing pipeline (owner: Priya Desai, due: 2026-03-18) - enables root-cause identification for mixed traffic
A3: Implement an admit-check in scheduler to block kernel variant assignment when warmup_count < X or recent fallback_rate > 2% (owner: Jamal Nguyen, due: 2026-03-20) - safety gate
A4: Add deterministic unit + integration tests that simulate bursty mixed-length traffic for kernel-choice regressions (owner: Lin Zhao, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-25)
A5: Canary rollout plan for adjusted heuristics with automatic rollback on p95 degradation > 5% over baseline (owner: SRE on-call rotation, due: 2026-03-30)
A6: KV-cache warmup improvement: prefetch and pin first-KV-page for long-sequence assignments when kernel differs from historical assignment (owner: Miguel Torres, due: 2026-04-01)
A7: Post-deploy audit: replay 48h of production traffic against candidate heuristics in canary to estimate fallback risk (owner: Data Science - Ana Gomez, due: 2026-03-21)
A8: Update runbook with new checklist: check per-kernel seq-histogram, fallback_rate, and scheduler-weights diff (owner: On-call SRE lead, due: 2026-03-12)
notes: Trade-offs considered: conservative short-term rollback reduces throughput optimization for short-seq workloads but stops customer impact immediately.

We debated increasing the scheduler's warmup window vs. adding admit-check logic; decided to implement admit-check first because it requires fewer global config changes and supports incremental tuning.
Telemetry design choice: emit per-kernel seq-histogram as a high-cardinality metric with 1h rollup to avoid trace volume explosion; full sample traces retained for suspected windows.

Compliance: add audit log entry for any scheduler weight change (owner: Security & Compliance, due: 2026-03-28)
